intro: Welcome! Today you write in English: capital letters, full stops and question marks, your personal details and a simple form. Small things like a capital I make your writing look correct and easy to read. Warm-up: how do you write the English word for 'saya'?
teachingNotes: Capital letters: the first word of a sentence, the word I (always, even in the middle — unlike Indonesian 'saya'), names of people, places (Jalan Braga, Bandung, Indonesia) and nationalities (Indonesian). The most common error is writing everything in small letters, chat style: 'my name is budi and i live in bandung' → 'My name is Budi and I live in Bandung.'

Basic punctuation only: full stop at the end of a sentence, question mark at the end of a question, comma in lists and addresses (Jalan Braga 10, Bandung), apostrophe in I'm and What's. Don't teach colons, semicolons or other rules.
Details: email addresses in small letters with no spaces (@ and . in the right place); phone numbers grouped so they are easy to read; from abroad, +62 replaces the first 0 (0812… → +62 812…).

Forms: first name = nama depan, surname = nama belakang / nama keluarga, date of birth (DOB) as day/month/year in Indonesia and the UK (the USA writes month/day/year). Paper forms often ask for BLOCK CAPITALS, except the email and the signature. Many Indonesians have only one name: forms differ, so tell the learner to follow the form's instructions or ask.
Limits (A0): no past tense (don't teach 'I was born…' — use the 'Date of birth' field instead), no simple present beyond fixed chunks like 'I live in…'. Keep sentences short.

keyPoints.title: Capital letters and punctuation
keyPoints.explanation: Use a capital letter for the first word of a sentence, the word I, names and places. End a sentence with a full stop (.) and a question with a question mark (?).

examples.en: My name is Budi and I live in Bandung.
examples.id: Nama saya Budi dan saya tinggal di Bandung.

keyPoints.title: Writing your details
keyPoints.explanation: Names and places start with a capital letter. Email addresses are written in small letters with no spaces. Group phone numbers so they are easy to read.

email: huruf kecil semua, tanpa spasi

keyPoints.title: Filling in a form
keyPoints.explanation: First name is your own name, surname is your family name. Write your date of birth as day/month/year.

blocks.text: Use a **capital letter** for: the **first word** of a sentence, the word **I** (always, even in the middle of a sentence), **names** of people (Budi, Sari), **places** (Jalan Braga, Bandung, Indonesia) and **nationalities** (Indonesian). Most of these rules are the same in Indonesian — the new one is **I**.

id.text: Pakai **huruf kapital** untuk: **kata pertama** kalimat, kata **I** (selalu, bahkan di tengah kalimat), **nama** orang (Budi, Sari), **tempat** (Jalan Braga, Bandung, Indonesia) dan **kebangsaan** (Indonesian). Sebagian besar aturan ini sama dengan bahasa Indonesia — yang baru adalah **I**.

rows.en: My name is Budi and I live in Bandung.
rows.id: Nama saya Budi dan saya tinggal di Bandung.
rows.note: not: my name is budi and i live in bandung

rows.en: This is Pak Hasan from Medan.

blocks.text: In chat apps people often type everything in small letters. In emails, forms and at work, use capitals — especially **I**. A small 'i' looks like a mistake.

id.text: Di aplikasi chat orang sering mengetik semuanya dengan huruf kecil. Di email, formulir dan pekerjaan, pakai huruf kapital — terutama **I**. Huruf 'i' kecil terlihat seperti kesalahan.

blocks.prompt: Which words need a capital letter? my teacher is pak hasan.
blocks.explain: My is the first word, and Pak Hasan is a person's name (with his title). Teacher is a normal word.

id.explain: My kata pertama, dan Pak Hasan nama orang (dengan sapaannya). Teacher kata biasa.

blocks.text: End a sentence with a **full stop** (.) and a question with a **question mark** (?). Use a **comma** (,) between items in a list and between parts of an address. The **apostrophe** (') shows letters are missing: I'm = I am, What's = What is.

id.text: Akhiri kalimat dengan **full stop** (titik .) dan pertanyaan dengan **question mark** (tanda tanya ?). Pakai **comma** (koma ,) di antara isi daftar dan di antara bagian alamat. **Apostrophe** (') menandai huruf yang hilang: I'm = I am, What's = What is.

rows.en: I have a pen, a book and a bag.
rows.id: Saya punya pulpen, buku dan tas.

blocks.prompt: Choose the end mark: How old are you_
blocks.explain: It's a question, so it ends with a question mark.

id.explain: Ini pertanyaan, jadi diakhiri tanda tanya.

blocks.text: **Names** and **places** start with a capital letter. Write an **address** like this: street and number, then a comma, then the city and postcode. Write an **email address** in small letters with no spaces. Write a **phone number** in small groups so it is easy to read.

id.text: **Nama** dan **tempat** diawali huruf kapital. Tulis **alamat** seperti ini: nama jalan dan nomor, lalu koma, lalu kota dan kode pos. Tulis **alamat email** dengan huruf kecil tanpa spasi. Tulis **nomor telepon** dalam kelompok kecil supaya mudah dibaca.

rows.id: alamat: jalan dan kota diawali kapital, koma sebelum kota
email: huruf kecil semua, tanpa spasi
nomor yang sama dari luar negeri: 0 di depan diganti +62

blocks.text: Check every detail twice. One wrong letter in an email address or one wrong digit in a phone number means nobody can contact you.

id.text: Periksa setiap data dua kali. Satu huruf salah di alamat email atau satu angka salah di nomor telepon membuat orang tidak bisa menghubungimu.

blocks.prompt: Which email address is written correctly?
blocks.explain: Email addresses use small letters, no spaces, and a dot (not a comma) before com.

id.explain: Alamat email memakai huruf kecil, tanpa spasi, dan titik (bukan koma) sebelum com.

blocks.text: Forms at a hotel, a school, a gym or an embassy use the same words. **First name** is your own name; **surname** (or *last name*, *family name*) is your family name. Write your **date of birth** as **day/month/year** (17/08/1998) — like in Indonesia. Paper forms often say **BLOCK CAPITALS**: write all the letters as capitals, except your email and your signature.

id.text: Formulir di hotel, sekolah, tempat gym atau kedutaan memakai kata-kata yang sama. **First name** adalah nama dirimu; **surname** (atau *last name*, *family name*) adalah nama keluarga. Tulis **date of birth** (tanggal lahir) sebagai **hari/bulan/tahun** (17/08/1998) — sama seperti di Indonesia. Formulir kertas sering meminta **BLOCK CAPITALS**: tulis semua huruf dengan kapital, kecuali email dan tanda tangan.

blocks.text: Careful with dates on American forms: the USA writes **month/day/year**, so 17 August 1998 is 08/17/1998. If you're not sure, write the month as a word: 17 August 1998.

id.text: Hati-hati dengan tanggal di formulir Amerika: Amerika Serikat menulis **bulan/hari/tahun**, jadi 17 Agustus 1998 ditulis 08/17/1998. Kalau ragu, tulis bulannya dengan kata: 17 August 1998.

blocks.prompt: Your name is Andi Wijaya. First name: ___
blocks.explain: First name is your own name: Andi. Wijaya goes in the Surname box.

id.explain: First name adalah nama dirimu: Andi. Wijaya ditulis di kotak Surname.

id.intro: Selamat datang! Hari ini kamu menulis dalam bahasa Inggris: huruf kapital, titik dan tanda tanya, data pribadimu, dan formulir sederhana. Hal kecil seperti huruf I kapital membuat tulisanmu terlihat benar dan mudah dibaca. Pemanasan: bagaimana kamu menulis kata bahasa Inggris untuk 'saya'?
suggestedQuestions: Kenapa I selalu ditulis dengan huruf kapital?
Di mana aku menaruh koma dalam alamat?
Apa yang kutulis di 'Surname' kalau namaku cuma satu kata?
Bagaimana menulis tanggal lahirku di formulir?

assessment.wb-4: Dengarkan. Tulis nomor telepon yang kamu dengar.
assessment.wb-5: Tulis alamat email ini seperti saat kamu mengetiknya: budiman at yahoo dot com
